rules.statement: Obligations run only with a Permit; denied requests consume no rate-limit quota (P15).

Each document's rate limit rules count in buckets of their own (the platform's by rule id, an app's and a tenant's prefixed with the document), so a tenant rule never spends, replaces or relaxes another document's: a tenant rule with a platform rule's id has its own counter, and the platform's rule still applies to the tenant's requests.

Every kind of obligation a permit carries is handled before the request proceeds; none is skipped. The pipeline dispatches on the sealed Obligation with an exhaustive when and no else, so a new kind does not compile until it is handled, and a model newer than the pipeline (version skew) fails the request with 500, never a permit.
guards: architecture:ObligationDispatchTest#obligations are dispatched by an exhaustive when without else
architecture:ObligationDispatchTest#no runtime code skips a kind of obligation

rules.source: RFC 0006 §8.4; #1229; round-2 review L1 and M3
rules.statement: The Redis rate limiter keeps each bucket in one key, `<prefix>:<rule>:<bucket>`, a hash of the window it counts in and that window's and the previous window's counts, and its script takes the time from Redis: it touches only the key it declares, so it runs on a Redis Cluster as on one node, and instances whose clocks differ count in the same window. A window ahead of Redis's clock keeps counting, never restarts. Every count leaves the key with an expiry of two windows, whatever the key held before. Different buckets are different keys, and spread over the slots.
